solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: High-flown sort of duck losing tail — it's flapping about

indicators.note: losing its tail means the last letter of the duck word is dropped

parts.note: Bombay duck is a kind of dried fish eaten in India

indicators.note: flapping suggests wild movement, so the letters of it's are jumbled

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A bird with a missing tail flaps around wildly in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing tail' cuts BOMBAY to BOMBA; 'flapping' turns ITS into STI. Bombay duck is not a bird at all but a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: High-flown language is pompous and inflated, just as bombastic speech is.

clue.text: Serving women made from Adam's rib

indicators.note: made from suggests a new thing fashioned from raw material, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eve was made from Adam's rib; here it is women who serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made from' rearranges ADAMS RIB; the Genesis story of Eve is the decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Barmaids are women who serve drinks in a pub.

clue.text: Chew lots, swallowing some number

indicators.note: swallowing means taking inside, so the number letter goes into the other word

parts.note: much means lots
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: Someone chews plenty of food, gulping down a quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: To munch is to eat noisily and steadily, which is chewing.

clue.text: Unity at home full of love: give me a squeeze!

parts.note: accord is agreement or unity

indicators.note: full of means holding something, so the home word wraps the love letter

parts.note: in means at home
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A harmonious, loving household asks for a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the instrument: an accordion is a squeezebox.
explanation.definitionFit: An accordion is played by squeezing its bellows, so it might well ask for a squeeze.

clue.text: Order of list corrected in article

indicators.note: in means the corrected letters sit inside the article

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: corrected means put right, so the letters of list are rearranged

explanation.surface: The order of names on a list has been fixed in a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrected' makes ISTL from LIST. The Order of the Thistle is Scotland's highest order of chivalry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thistle is short for the Most Ancient and Most Noble Order of the Thistle.

clue.text: Turner puts lid on brown

parts.note: caps means covers with a lid
tan is a light brown

explanation.surface: J. M. W. Turner tops a painting with brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter, but it is something that turns: a capstan is a revolving drum for winding rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is a rotating cylinder on a ship used to wind in cables.

clue.text: Witness, at the start, a return of colourful bird

indicators.note: at the start asks for just the opening letter of the word Witness
a return means the colour word is read backwards

parts.note: red is a colour, so colourful can give RED

explanation.surface: Someone sees a bright bird come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colourful bird' looks like the definition, but 'colourful' gives RED, which 'return of' turns into DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A wader is a long-legged wading bird such as a heron or stork.

clue.text: Puppy at first washed daily

indicators.note: at first takes just the first letter of washed

parts.note: a daily is a British term for a cleaner who comes in each day, a help

explanation.surface: A young dog is bathed every day.
explanation.definitionFit: A whelp is a young dog or other young carnivore.

clue.text: Policemen shoot as retort, perhaps

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors
a tiller is a new shoot growing from a plant's base

explanation.surface: Police officers open fire in response.
explanation.walkthrough: A retort is a glass vessel used in distilling, so it is one example of a distiller.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is laboratory apparatus for distilling liquids, so it may count as a distiller.

clue.text: Get back and think again

definitions.meaning: to regain or recover, as a pawned item
read as ..., to deem once more

explanation.surface: Reclaim something and reconsider.
explanation.definitionFit: Redeem means recover by payment, and split as re-deem means judge anew.

clue.text: Continuous period in charge of some letters

parts.note: a run is an unbroken spell, as in a run of good luck

explanation.surface: Someone holds responsibility for a batch of correspondence for a long spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Runic describes runes, the characters of an old Germanic alphabet.

clue.text: I manage papers! Wowed?

parts.note: the clue's I is read as the speaker saying I'M, I am
the press is the newspapers collectively
ED, an editor, is the one who manages a paper

explanation.surface: A boastful newspaper chief exclaims about their role, then asks whether anyone was amazed.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I manage papers' as the claim 'I'm press ed', that is, I am the press editor; run together it spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be impressed is to be struck with admiration, much as being wowed is.

clue.text: Being short of water initially hard for female

indicators.note: hard for female means the letter for female is swapped out and hard's letter put in

parts.note: at first means initially
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Thirst first came on hard for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letter signal, but it is the phrase AT FIRST; 'for' swaps its F for H.
explanation.definitionFit: Athirst is an old word for thirsty, lacking a drink.

clue.text: Cut current, restricting theatrical events

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the current word closes around the other piece

parts.note: a tide is a flow of water, a current
ops, surgical operations, are carried out in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: A power cut stopped shows at a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatrical' means the operating theatre, not the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Topside is a lean cut of beef from the upper hindquarters.

clue.text: Go through cases, then happen to find novel

parts.note: to decline a noun is to recite its grammatical cases
and can mean then, as in 'and then'
to fall is to happen, as in 'Easter falls in April'

explanation.surface: Working through legal cases, someone stumbles on a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Decline and Fall is Evelyn Waugh's first novel (1928).
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the title of a well-known comic novel by Evelyn Waugh.

clue.text: Helping with party, working out expense of protecting house

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so the house letters sit inside

parts.note: costing is calculating what something costs

explanation.surface: A party planner budgets carefully while guarding a property.
explanation.definitionFit: Cohosting is jointly running an event, sharing the hosting duties.

clue.text: Encrypting files gave minimum concealment

indicators.note: encrypting scrambles a message, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Coding computer files provided the barest protection.
explanation.definitionFit: In art, fig leaves cover only the genitals of nude figures, the least possible modesty.

clue.text: Fine description of Quidditch? It can reasonably be attacked

definitions.meaning: a sporting contest played justly, Quidditch being the wizard sport in Harry Potter
a legitimate target for criticism or pursuit

explanation.surface: A well-played Quidditch match is open to criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a just contest and a legitimate target for attack.

clue.text: Animator has gap to fix in dreamlike sequence

indicators.note: fixing here means rearranging into order, so the letters of these words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A cartoon maker must patch a hole in a dream scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantasmagoria is a shifting series of real or imagined images, as in a dream.

clue.text: Headings of analyst's ring binder that should shed some light

indicators.note: headings are the first letters of the following words

parts.note: a clamp binds things tightly together

explanation.surface: An analyst's ring binder holds notes that should explain things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring binder' looks like one item; 'ring' gives only its first letter and 'binder' is CLAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc lamp produces bright light from an electric arc between electrodes.

clue.text: Teach me to develop into a hacker

indicators.note: develop means evolve into something new, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trainee asks to be taught to become a computer hacker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to develop' rearranges TEACH ME; 'hacker' is not computing but a hacking blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy knife used to hack through vegetation.

clue.text: Was quick to take in a chapter, leaving gaps

indicators.note: to take in means to contain, so the speed word wraps the other pieces

parts.note: sped means went fast, was quick

explanation.surface: A reader rushes through a chapter, skipping parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaced means arranged with intervals between, leaving gaps.

clue.text: Letters make opening of conversation academic

parts.note: post is letters delivered by mail
do can mean make, as in 'do a cake'

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Mail can start a dialogue between scholars.
explanation.definitionFit: A postdoc is a researcher in a post after completing a doctorate.

clue.text: Mild curse when having to keep following bank order

indicators.note: having to keep means holding, so the curse surrounds the letter

parts.note: drat is a mild curse
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Someone mutters an oath when made to obey a banking instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank draft is an order for payment drawn by a bank.

clue.text: Possibly one who narrowly escapes cold, with radiator

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a radiator is a kind of heater

explanation.surface: Someone narrowly avoids a chill by sitting by a radiator.
explanation.walkthrough: One who cheats death has a narrow escape; 'Possibly' flags this as only one kind of cheater.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cheats death survives by a whisker, so is a cheater of a sort.

clue.text: Spine damaged, put in hospital

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the hospital letter goes within

parts.note: torn means damaged by ripping
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: An injured spine lands someone in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spine' suggests the backbone, but it is a plant's prickle.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a sharp spine on a plant stem.

clue.text: Where one bravely takes misfortune, conscious it may provide a service

parts.note: one stoically takes a blow on the chin
aware means conscious

explanation.surface: A brave sufferer, knowing their fate, still serves others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' is a set of crockery, a tea or dinner service.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain tableware can make up a matching dinner set.

clue.text: One takes a bow — girl pretending to be a boy

definitions.meaning: a stringed instrument played with a bow

definitions.text: girl pretending to be a boy
definitions.meaning: ... disguises herself as the youth Cesario in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night

explanation.surface: A cross-dressing actress takes her curtain call.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a bowed instrument and Shakespeare's disguised heroine.

clue.text: Figure I had rejected a fool

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the shortened I had is reversed

parts.note: I'd is short for I had
git is British slang for a stupid person

explanation.surface: Someone admits they turned down a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is a numeral, a single figure from 0 to 9.

clue.text: Requests one to leave a nice, secluded part of garden

parts.note: pleas are appeals or requests

indicators.note: one to leave means the letter for one is dropped

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Pleas for someone to vacate a pleasant, quiet corner of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' drops I from A NICE, leaving ANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasance is an old term for a secluded pleasure garden or enclosure.
